name: Privacy-preserving cryptocurrency selection
description: The adversary applies a structured evaluation framework when selecting a cryptocurrency for anonymous transactions, assessing: (1) mandatory vs. optional privacy configuration; (2) cryptographic privacy mechanism (ring signatures+CT, zk-SNARKs, Mimblewimble, shielded pools); (3) resistance to blockchain analysis; (4) quantum resistance; (5) exchange exposure creating KYC attribution vectors.

subtechniques.name: Prefer mandatory-privacy cryptocurrencies
subtechniques.description: Cryptocurrencies where all transactions are private by default provide stronger anonymity than optional-privacy systems. Optional-privacy currencies have small anonymity sets because most users use transparent transactions, making the private subset conspicuous.

subtechniques.name: Evaluate cryptographic privacy mechanism
subtechniques.description: Different privacy cryptocurrencies use different cryptographic techniques: ring signatures+CT (Monero) for unlinkability and amount hiding; zk-SNARKs (Zcash, Aleo) requiring trusted setup; Mimblewimble (Grin, Beam) with good pruning but limited scripting. The adversary evaluates specific mechanisms for known weaknesses and law enforcement bypass capabilities.
